narrativeProgression.description: David Cobb asks Kshama Sawant if she sees the Green Party's principles as an umbrella she could be comfortable with
Kshama Sawant agrees with the Green Party's principles and believes most working and young people do too
She highlights the challenge of bringing people together to fight for social change
Kshama Sawant contrasts their high agreement with the Green Party to their vast disagreement with Democrats and Republicans
David Cobb agrees and emphasizes the need to work together while acknowledging disagreements

text_to_speech: I do want to actually push uh and ask do you see the green party's principles values the four pillars of the international Green Party Movement uh peace Justice democracy ecology do you see that as an umbrella that you could be comfortable with uh going forward not only in 2016 but beyond but I think that all the values that you mentioned as the four pillars of the green party are are aspects not only that I agree or socialist alternative agrees but I think the vast majority of what people and young people agree on this I don't think that there's anything controversial about that I think our challenge moving forward and I think we are completely capable as as not only organizations but as people on the ground working people on the ground history shows us that we have the ability to bring these forces together and really fight for social change I mean you know when you were saying well if you agree on 95% of the things it just made me realize oh and and imagine imagine how much we disagree on with the Democrats and Republicans you know right it's probably 99.9% of the time you know we we disagree with them and so I think that that that uh formulation of how we we do have massive agreement let's work together while being open about our disagreements is the best way in which we can actually bring working people to the struggle because ultimately you know uh we can have as many discussions and debates as we want among people who are you know seasoned activists people who spent many years being in political struggle but there is no hope for us to bring any of that agenda of Peace Justice you know economic Justice economic democracy and and ecological uh Freedom all of that uh into fruition unless the masses of working people come with us and fight on the streets and they will but we need to empower them

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I do want to actually push and ask, do you see the Green Party's principles, values, the
four pillars of the International Green Party movement, peace, justice, democracy, ecology?
Do you see that as an umbrella that you could be comfortable with going forward, not only
in 2016 but beyond?
Well, I think that all the values that you mentioned as the four pillars of the Green Party are
aspects not only that I agree or socialists alternative agrees, but I think the vast majority
of working people and young people agree on this.
I don't think that there's anything controversial about that.
I think our challenge moving forward and I think we are completely capable as not only organizations
but as people on the ground, working people on the ground.
History shows us that we have the ability to bring these forces together and really fight
for social change.
I mean, you know, when you were saying, well, if you agree on 95% of the things, it just
made me realize, oh, well, and imagine how much we disagree on with the Democrats and
Republicans, you know, it's probably 99.9% of time, you know, we disagree with them.
And so I think that that formulation of how we do have massive agreement, let's work together
while being open about our disagreements is the best way in which we can actually bring
working people to the struggle.
And ultimately, you know, we can have as many discussions and debates as we want among
people who are, you know, seasoned activists, people who have spent many years being in political
struggle, but there is no hope for us to bring any of that agenda of peace, justice, you
know, economic justice, the economic democracy and ecological freedom, all of that into fruition
unless the masses of working people come with us and fight on the streets and they will,
but we need to empower them.

youtube_description:
Stein/Baraka campaign manager David Cobb sat down with Socialist Alternative spokesperson Kshama Sawant to ask what might stop left-wing groups from coalescing around the Green Party's 2016 presidential ticket.
